escalations.why_a_human_must_decide: Operations marked the account closed and sites inactive without an attached customer termination notice, while the signed agreement says a system inactive status does not replace a termination notice.
A transfer of routes and account relationships is described, but the signed agreement requires prior written customer consent and the pack does not contain that consent.

An internal rate table is approved for billing preparation, including a Quarry Tower change to GBP 24.67, while the signed agreement says a revised price takes effect only through a written change signed by both parties; customer signature and amendment fields are blank.

INV-2025-069 prints due on receipt, 8.7 percent yearly interest and a GBP 58.71 recovery charge, while the signed agreement prints 30 days, 4.6 percent and no fixed recovery fee, and says a shorter term on a later invoice changes the agreement only if both parties sign an amendment.

The corrected certificate and review headline carry 20.415 t and 3761 Nm³ while the same review's detailed schedule carries 20.405 t and 3763 Nm³; a human must decide which published figure is issued to the customer.
Container count for WT-GL-SH-MAR-Q7N is 2 on the final ticket, the register, the CSV and the customer review, and 3 on the weigh-ticket index table and its transcription note.
The treatment invoice description states 1.091 tonnes while the quantity column states 1.137 t; both cannot be billed as the quantity without a human choice.
Finance has a June 2025 billing draft of 52 visits while the register records the account closed at the end of May and sites inactive; a human must decide whether a June invoice may be issued.
Operations announce a September 2025 restart of two sites and issue INV-2025-086 after the same operations file has entered a closed status without customer notice.
The visit labelled Hearth with blank site_code shares a ticket-reference prefix HO with Hearth office; the customer review forbids collapsing the unassigned label.
Estimated kilograms are published beside weighed kilograms; a human must keep those statuses apart if a later system would treat billed or certified mass as weighed.
